_comment: Binding metadata for the hooks in this directory. A hook script cannot
declare its own event, so scripts/install-hooks.py reads it from here.
Each entry: the script's filename, the harness event it binds to, an
optional tool matcher, an optional `if` permission-rule prefilter (which
keeps the hook from spawning on every unrelated call), and a one-line
reason naming the rule it enforces.

hooks.why: CLAUDE.md 'Timestamp recaps in local time' -- supplies the real local time each turn, because a fabricated timestamp is indistinguishable from a remembered one.

_note_no_if: Deliberately carries no `if` prefilter. `Bash(gh *)` was tried and
verified working in the live harness -- it fires on `cd /tmp && gh ...`
and on `GH_TOKEN=x gh ...`, so it is not a strict prefix glob today.
It is still removed, because the asymmetry is bad: if that matching
ever tightens to a prefix check, the guard stops firing on exactly the
compound and env-prefixed shapes it exists to catch, and it stops
SILENTLY -- a disabled guard and a guard with nothing to block look
identical. The prefilter buys one Python startup (~30ms) per gh-less
Bash call; that is not worth a silent-failure mode.
hooks.why: Blocks mutating repo-scoped gh commands lacking -R, so a write never silently targets whatever repo the cwd happens to be.
report-mistakes-proactively 'Filing is not gated on approval' -- blocks a reply that offers to file or record instead of doing it.
Blocks a reply asserting a PR's check state when the last status query predates the last push, so a stale reading is never reported as current.

_note_warns_never_blocks: Emits `additionalContext` and a `systemMessage` and nothing else --
no `permissionDecision` key at all, so the normal permission flow is
untouched. Naming `allow` there would BYPASS a prompt the user would
otherwise have seen, which is a hook making the harness more
permissive than it was without it.
Deny was considered and rejected on the numbers: 60 of 121 real Agent
launches in this machine's transcripts are write-capable with no
`isolation`, so a blocking guard would interrupt 49% of agent
launches. The lapse it catches is a visibility failure, and a warning
at the moment of the call fixes visibility completely.
NOT REGISTERED on any machine yet. Activation is a separate decision
after review -- run scripts/install-hooks.py --fix to opt in.
hooks.why: Surfaces a write-capable Agent launch with no `isolation`, so a decided practice cannot lapse silently -- the omission lives in a tool call, the one surface review, tests, and lint all miss.

_note_not_a_stop_hook: Deliberately UserPromptSubmit rather than Stop, which is the shape
the three guards above use. A Stop guard suppresses a message that is
wrong to send. An error admission is RIGHT to send: blocking it would
suppress the honest correction, delay it reaching the user, and remove
the very signal that surfaces the mistake. So this reminds on the next
prompt and can only ever ADD context -- there is no code path in it
that suppresses, delays, or alters a message.
hooks.why: CLAUDE.md 'Run UMS proactively' -- discovering you were wrong is a trigger with no artifact, so nothing else prompts the pass; this injects a reminder naming the admitted error when no memory/skill write followed it.
report-mistakes-proactively 'Filing is not gated on approval' -- no-offer-to-file.py catches the OFFER (needs a `?`); this catches the DECLARATIVE form, which asks nothing and so slips past it.

cai 2026-08-02 'every time you make a mistake, write a hook to prevent it recurring'. Injects rather than blocks, because an error admission is RIGHT to send -- only the follow-up is owed. Complements remind-ums-after-error.py: that one wants a recorded learning, this one wants a mechanism.

CLAUDE.md 'Open a PR for every pushed feature branch' + skills/ardi 'always request another review' -- opening a PR auto-triggers the repo's own review workflow but does NOT summon Copilot, and that auto-triggered half is what disguises the missing one. claude-review has failed on every attempted review this session (ai-config#897, which calls the cause an unconfirmed leading hypothesis); whatever the cause, an unrequested PR gets no review at all while it is down.

shared/coding/ascii-punctuation-in-source.md's over-application warning. A whole-file glyph replace converts pre-existing glyphs on untouched lines, and the resulting mechanical diff HIDES real changes -- on 2026-08-02 it concealed two dropped paragraphs. Blocks only when a glyph replace, a write-back, and no scoping token all co-occur under an interpreter.

_note_covers_external_correction: UserPromptSubmit, inject-only, for the same reason as the two
reminders above: accepting a reviewer's finding and fixing it is
RIGHT, so this can only ADD context and never blocks. It fills the
hole those two leave -- both key on a FIRST-PERSON admission and
else, so agreeing with a reviewer triggers neither. That is the
commonest way a mistake surfaces and the class ai-config#1065 is
NOT REGISTERED on any machine yet. Activation is a separate decision
after this PR merges (README's activation gate) -- run
scripts/install-hooks.py --fix to opt in then, not before.
hooks.why: ai-config#1065 'any time a reviewer brings up valid concerns, learn from that'. Injects, never blocks, when an accepted reviewer finding has no recorded learning or mechanism after it -- the external-correction sibling of remind-ums-after-error.py, which fires only on first-person admissions.
